summary.text: Andrew Harris is the Republican incumbent seeking re-election in Maryland's 1st Congressional District. A physician and Naval Reserve medical officer, he served 12 years in the Maryland State Senate before his election to Congress in 2010. He chairs the House Freedom Caucus and sits on the House Appropriations Committee.

paragraphs.text: Harris was born January 25, 1957, in Brooklyn, New York, the son of immigrants from Eastern Europe, according to his official biography.
He earned a B.S. (1977) and M.D. (1980) from Johns Hopkins University and an M.H.S. from Johns Hopkins in 1995.
He worked as a physician at the Johns Hopkins Hospital for nearly three decades, specializing as an anesthesiologist in obstetric anesthesia.

Harris joined the U.S. Naval Reserve in 1988 as a medical officer, established and commanded the Johns Hopkins Medical Naval Reserve Unit, and was called to active duty in 1990 for Operation Desert Shield and Desert Storm at Bethesda Naval Hospital.
He reached the rank of Commander and left the Reserves after seventeen years.
He was elected to the Maryland State Senate in 1998 and served 12 years; Wikipedia lists him as minority whip from 2003 to 2006.
First elected to the U.S. House in 2010, he has represented Maryland's 1st District since January 2011.

In the House, Harris serves on the Appropriations Committee, chairing its Subcommittee on Agriculture, Rural Development, Food and Drug Administration, and Related Agencies and serving on the Labor, Health and Human Services, Education subcommittee.
An original member of the House Freedom Caucus, he was elected its chairman on September 17, 2024.

According to his official biography, he was married to his late wife, Cookie, for over 33 years, has five children, one stepchild and ten grandchildren, and lives in Dorchester County with his wife Nicole.
